- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward momentum.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap forecast decline to 5–10% below peak unless sentiment shifts strongly bullish.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to recognize mean reversion; adjust forecast to align with 3–5 day moving average of prior 10–15 days.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overreact to recent sentiment swings; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 5-day weighted average) to reduce noise.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misjudges turning points; use sentiment momentum (last 3 days) to adjust forecast directionality.
